text:
maya: Heads-up — procurement just flagged a possible 6–10 week customs delay for H200 racks entering the EU. Need to re-evaluate our Q2 capacity plan and fallbacks.

ajay: Ugh, ok. Is this for a specific carrier/port or a general delay trend?

maya: It's concentrated on Hamburg/Rotterdam lanes for one supplier (ETA shifts on their manifest). Procurement says backlog at port could add 3w, customs paperwork another 2–4w.

liam: If H200s slip, can we temporarily shift workload to L40S in eu-west-1? latency/cost tradeoffs?

sara: Quick math: our Q2 forecast needs ~1.2M GPU-hours. H200s give ~2.4x throughput per GPU vs L40S for large-context batch inference. If we reroute 25% of H200 hours to L40S, we'd need ~2.5x more L40S hours for those jobs -> big cost/slot impact.

maya: Right. Options I see: 1) accelerate H100 roll-in (shorter lead times), 2) shift L40S from US pools to EU (network + syncing), 3) buy short-term burst on cloud region, 4) prioritize customer-facing routes and degrade noncritical workloads.

procurement-bot: procurement update: vendor A confirmed manifest shift: 40 H200 units delayed, new ETA candidate windows: 2026-05-08 to 2026-06-12.

ajay: Can we take a mixed approach: move lower-QPS batch jobs to L40S in eu-west-1 and reserve burst capacity in dedicated US pool that can failover? Concern: KV-cache replication latency across regions could spike token latency > SLO. :thinking:

liam: We can limit cross-region failover to non-interactive jobs (embeddings, offline evals). Interactive chat traffic must remain local. Also check whether our prefix caching survives model variant swap (H200 -> H100/H100-ql).

maya: Good call. Also procurement suggests negotiating partial shipments to avoid the whole manifest hitting customs at once. Ask vendor for staggered manifests and digital customs docs ahead of shipments.

procurement-bot: Suggested ask to vendor: stagger shipments weekly, provide full EORI/KD docs 10 days prior. Vendor open to 2-week stagger.

ajay: From ops side, I'll sketch a fallback routing policy:
```
route_policy {
  priority: [local-h200, local-h100, regional-l40s, cross-region-burst]
  degrade_conditions: [queue_depth>500, p99_latency>350ms]
  repin_models: true
}
```

sara: Also ran a quick cost delta: swapping 20% H200-hours -> L40S in EU raises expected token cost ~+38% and increases GPU-hour need by ~2.2x for that slice. But saves ~6 weeks of wait if we can source L40S quickly.

liam: Can we use quantized H200 variants (H200-8bit) to stretch capacity in the near term? That might reduce throughput per GPU but reduce memory pressure and let more replicas fit per rack.

maya: Procurement confirmed H100 lead time is ~3–5 weeks and H100 shipments are more flexible. If we accelerate an H100 tranche, we could offset some H200 hours while keeping latency closer to target.

ajay: Network note: shifting L40S from US to EU requires re-sync of model cache (~2–3 hours per host for large model tarballs). Need maintenance windows or warm-burst prefetch.

maya: Action items: @ajay draft routing policy and failover whitelist for non-interactive jobs by EOD Tue. @sara produce a Q2 revised GPU-hours table with cost delta for 3 scenarios (staggered H200, accelerated H100 purchase, L40S-shift + cloud-burst) by Wed. @procurement-bot continue negotiating staggered manifests and weekly partials; report back with confirmed ETAs. I'll coordinate with CS to prioritize customer routes. :shipit:

infra-bot: NOTE: queued capacity rebinds may require a rolling restart of serving pools; expect brief throttling while caches rebuild.

ajay: Ack — will include rolling-restart windows in the plan.

maya: Thanks all. Let's reconvene after the revised numbers.

procurement-bot: logged: case-#8793 — vendor stagger request sent.
